key_insight: This paper proposes a training-free way to reduce medical MLLM hallucinations by injecting verifiable anatomical evidence into both visual perception and text reasoning.
clinical_relevance: It could make clinical VQA and radiology report generation more trustworthy by better aligning model answers with image evidence.
method: Use MedSAM-derived ROI priors to modulate visual activations around relevant anatomy.
Convert anatomical coordinates into discrete semantic tokens to serve as verifiable external memory.
Add a task-aware router to choose perception-side or reasoning-side interventions based on the query.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 2 tasks and 5 datasets with LLaVA-1.5-7B, LLaVA-Med-1.5-7B, Qwen3-VL, and InternVL, showing up to ~6% higher closed-ended accuracy and ~35% lower open-ended hallucinations.
watch_item: The framework depends on reliable ROI extraction and coordinate grounding, so performance may vary if anatomical priors are inaccurate or hard to obtain in real clinical workflows.
paper_title: Synergistic Perception-Reasoning Governance: Grounding Medical MLLMs with Verifiable Anatomical Evidence
